html:
Double bomb attack by the Provisional IRA on British soldiers near Warrenpoint, County Down, on 27 August 1979. It killed 18 soldiers, the British Army's worst single loss of the Troubles.

A bomb hidden in a lorry full of straw blew up beside an army convoy on the road at Narrow Water, killing six members of the Parachute Regiment. Reinforcements and a helicopter came to the scene. The IRA, watching from across the water in the Republic, set off a second, larger bomb at the place where the soldiers had gathered. Twelve more died, including the Queen's Own Highlanders' commanding officer.

The attack came the same day as the killing of Lord Mountbatten, and the two together gave the government a hard week. See the-troubles.
